name: Permanent Residence (Autorização de Residência Permanente)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires 5 years of temporary residence — this requirement was NOT changed by the 2026 nationality reform, unlike the naturalisation timeline, which is a genuinely important distinction to keep straight.
This requires Portuguese at A2 (CIPLE) — CPLP nationals are exempt.
requirements.fix_path: Take the CIPLE exam at A2, unless CPLP-exempt.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires no serious criminal convictions in the last 5 years (cumulatively exceeding 1 year in prison).
This requires not exceeding 6 months' absence in any single year, or 12 consecutive months overall, during the qualifying period.
This requires being up to date on tax and social security obligations, plus demonstrated subsistence means.

evidence_required.document: 5 years of continuous residence evidence, including full absence history
Up-to-date tax and social security records

sources.title: AIMA — Autorização de Residência Permanente, Art. 80.º

notes: Portugal's ILR/Niederlassungserlaubnis-equivalent hub route, same structural role as uk_ilr, de_niederlassungserlaubnis, and nl_permanent_residence — every major feeder route in this dataset resolves through here. GENUINE, IMPORTANT DISTINCTION worth surfacing prominently: the 5-year PR residence requirement was NOT touched by the 2026 nationality reform — only the SEPARATE naturalisation-specific clock was extended to 7/10 years. This means someone can reach Portuguese permanent residence at 5 years exactly as before, but then must wait an ADDITIONAL 2 years (CPLP/EU) or 5 years (others) beyond that before naturalising — citizenship_after_months here is set to 24 (the CPLP/EU case) rather than 0, unlike every other country's PR-hub route in this dataset (UK ILR, Germany's Niederlassungserlaubnis, NL's permanent residence permit) where reaching PR and being naturalisation-eligible are effectively the same moment. This is a genuinely distinctive two-stage structure worth highlighting in any 'time to citizenship' comparison view — Portugal looks fast on paper (5-year PR) but the REAL total time to citizenship (84 months / 7 years minimum) is now comparable to or slower than some of the other three countries, a finding that directly contradicts Portugal's popular reputation as Europe's fastest citizenship route. Fee (grant €351.10 / renewal-equivalent data change €61.90) confirmed via the AIMA fee table.
